subject: Media Literacy
title: What Is Misinformation
description: A fast breakdown of What Is Misinformation for builders.

hook.text: A fake article claimed Pope Francis endorsed a presidential candidate. Over a million people shared it.

buildup.text: Misinformation is false or inaccurate information spread without intent to deceive — often by mistake.

discovery.text: It differs from disinformation, which is deliberately created to mislead, and malinformation, which is true but harmful.

twist.text: Most people who spread misinformation believe it's true. The spreaders are victims too, not just accomplices.

climax.text: Understanding the difference between mis-, dis-, and malinformation helps you identify the right response.

punchline.text: Not all false info is malicious. But it's all dangerous.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between misinformation and disinformation?
options: Misinformation is spread without intent to deceive; disinformation is deliberate
